policy_title: Introduce Proportional Representation for the House of Commons
stated: Reform UK will introduce Proportional Representation voting for the House of Commons, stating that large numbers of voters are unrepresented and new parties are shut out, which they believe could increase voter turnout. A referendum is needed for this change.

source.quote: Proportional Representation Voting for the House of Commons Large numbers of voters have no representation in parliament and new parties are shut out of the political system. Voter turnout could be some 10% higher with PR. A referendum is needed.

bearing_set.reason: Changing the electoral system for the House of Commons directly affects voting and democratic rights — how votes translate into representation — which falls squarely within O9's explicit scope of 'voting & democratic rights'.

The policy explicitly targets voter turnout; research on PR systems links more proportional representation to higher civic participation (a direct O15 indicator) via the concrete mechanism that fewer 'wasted' votes increases perceived democratic efficacy and engagement.

membership_note: The primary bearing is firmly O9 (democratic rights/equal treatment); O15 earns a real verdict because the policy names voter turnout as a goal and civic participation is a listed O15 indicator with a nameable mechanism. No other fundamental clears the non-negligible bar: fiscal cost of a referendum is trivial (not O12), and effects on economic outcomes or personal liberty are too indirect and diffuse to pin to a specific indicator.
